docs.title: Myyaml
docs.text: Myyaml is a small, dependency-free YAML 1.2 implementation for C++17 and C11. It provides deterministic round trips, strict validation and parse errors with source positions.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
#include <myyaml/myyaml.hpp>

#include <iostream>

int main()
{
    myyaml::yaml config = myyaml::yaml::parse(
        "name: demo\n"
        "enabled: true\n"
        "ports: [8080, 8081]\n");

    std::cout << config["name"].as_string() << '\n';

    myyaml::dump_options options;
    options.sort_keys = true;
    std::cout << config.dump(options);
}

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• Usage — parsing, reading, emitting, building documents and limits.
  • C API — opaque handles, ownership, error state and examples.
  • Tests and benchmarks — Catch2 test and benchmark targets.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text: The implementation covers block and flow collections, quoted and block scalars, comments, document markers, anchors/aliases and the YAML 1.2 core schema. Multi-document streams, complex keys, recursive aliases and arbitrary tag resolution are not supported. See REVIEW.md for known limitations and IMPROVE.md for planned work.

docs.title: Tests and benchmarks
docs.text: Both the unit tests and the microbenchmarks use Catch2. Catch2 is vendored as a submodule under tests/vendor/Catch2; if it is missing, CMake fetches it with FetchContent.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DMYYAML_BUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DMYYAML_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON
cmake --build build

docs.title: Run the unit tests
docs.text:
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

The C++ and C suites are separate executables, so individual tests can also be selected through Catch2:

./build/tests/myyaml-cpp-tests "block scalars"
./build/tests/myyaml-c-tests "[c][parse]"

docs.title: Run the benchmarks
docs.text:
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks

Catch2 prints the mean, confidence interval and standard deviation for each benchmark. The executable accepts the standard Catch2 benchmark options:

# Faster iteration while developing
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks \
  --benchmark-samples 10 \
  --benchmark-resamples 1000 \
  --benchmark-warmup-time 20

# Run only parser, emitter, round-trip or C API benchmarks
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks "[parser]"
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks "[emitter]"
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks "[roundtrip]"
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks "[c-api]"

# Disable statistical analysis for the raw sample mean
./build/benchmarks/myyaml-benchmarks --benchmark-no-analysis

ctest --test-dir build -L benchmark runs the benchmark suite with a reduced sample count for CI.

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text:
The benchmarks use a small hand-written configuration, a flow-style document, an anchor/alias document, a 1000-element sequence, a 256-key mapping and a generated large nested service configuration.

Group Scenarios [parser] scalar, small block, flow, anchors/aliases, long sequence, mapping, large config [emitter] scalar, block, flow, sorted/indented, large config block and flow [roundtrip] parse + dump, lookup, mapping insert, sequence append [c-api] parse and parse + dump through the C wrapper

The numbers are comparative rather than absolute. Run benchmarks in a Release build on an otherwise idle machine, and compare results from the same machine and compiler. Benchmarking a Debug build measures debug STL and assertion overhead, not the library's typical performance.

docs.title: C API
docs.text:
The C API is a thin, exception-free wrapper around the C++ implementation. It uses opaque handles and reports failures through status codes and a thread-local error state.

Include the header and link Myyaml::MyyamlC:

#include <myyaml/myyaml.h>

find_package(Myyaml REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE Myyaml::MyyamlC)

docs.title: Parse and read
docs.text:
#include <myyaml/myyaml.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

int main(void)
{
    myyaml_document *document = myyaml_parse(
        "name: demo\n"
        "enabled: true\n"
        "items:\n"
        "  - one\n"
        "  - 2\n");
    if (document == NULL)
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "parse failed: %s\n", myyaml_last_error());
        return 1;
    }

    const myyaml_node *root = myyaml_const_root(document);
    const myyaml_node *name = myyaml_node_get(root, "name");
    const myyaml_node *items = myyaml_node_get(root, "items");

    printf("name: %s\n", myyaml_node_get_string(name));
    printf("items: %zu\n", myyaml_node_size(items));
    printf("first: %s\n", myyaml_node_get_string(myyaml_node_at(items, 0)));

    myyaml_free(document);
    return 0;
}

Use myyaml_parse_n() when the input is not NUL-terminated or may contain NUL bytes, and myyaml_parse_with_options() to apply parser limits:

myyaml_parse_options options;
memset(&options, 0, sizeof(options));
options.max_depth = 64;
options.max_input_size = 1024 * 1024;
options.max_nodes = 100000;

myyaml_document *document =
    myyaml_parse_with_options(text, text_length, &options);

Zero numeric fields select the library defaults. Boolean fields are interpreted literally.

docs.title: Read typed values
docs.text:
Type queries and getters never throw:

int enabled = 0;
if (myyaml_node_get_bool(myyaml_node_get(root, "enabled"), &enabled))
{
    printf("enabled: %d\n", enabled);
}

long long count = 0;
if (myyaml_node_get_integer(myyaml_node_get(root, "count"), &count))
{
    printf("count: %lld\n", count);
}

const char *text = myyaml_node_get_string(node);
size_t length = myyaml_node_string_length(node); /* keeps embedded NUL bytes */

A getter returns 0 on a type mismatch. myyaml_last_status() then remains MYYAML_STATUS_OK, because a mismatch is not an operation failure.

docs.title: Build a document
docs.text:
myyaml_document *document = myyaml_create();
myyaml_node *root = myyaml_root(document);

myyaml_node *name = myyaml_node_set_key(root, "name");
myyaml_node_set_string(name, "demo");

myyaml_node *ports = myyaml_node_set_key(root, "ports");
myyaml_node_set_integer(myyaml_node_append(ports), 8080);
myyaml_node_set_integer(myyaml_node_append(ports), 8081);

myyaml_node *features = myyaml_node_set_key(root, "features");
myyaml_node_set_string(myyaml_node_append(features), "parse");
myyaml_node_set_string(myyaml_node_append(features), "emit");

myyaml_node_set_key() converts a null node to a mapping and inserts the key with a null value if it is missing. myyaml_node_append() converts a null node to a sequence and appends a null element.

docs.title: Emit YAML
docs.text:
myyaml_dump_options options;
memset(&options, 0, sizeof(options));
options.indent = 2;
options.sort_keys = 1;
options.trailing_newline = 1;

char *text = myyaml_dump_with_options(document, &options);
if (text == NULL)
{
    fprintf(stderr, "dump failed: %s\n", myyaml_last_error());
}
else
{
    puts(text);
    myyaml_free_string(text);
}
myyaml_free(document);

The caller owns the returned string and must release it with myyaml_free_string(). The caller also owns documents created by myyaml_parse*() and myyaml_create(); release them with myyaml_free().

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
On failure, parse and build functions return NULL or 0 and store an error message. The error state is thread-local.

myyaml_document *document = myyaml_parse("a: [1, 2\n");
if (document == NULL)
{
    fprintf(stderr, "status: %d\n", (int)myyaml_last_status());
    fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", myyaml_last_error());
    fprintf(stderr, "at line %zu, column %zu, byte %zu\n",
            myyaml_last_error_line(),
            myyaml_last_error_column(),
            myyaml_last_error_index());
}

Status values are declared in myyaml_status. Parse failures use MYYAML_STATUS_PARSE_ERROR; invalid arguments use MYYAML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT; type mismatches during mutation use MYYAML_STATUS_TYPE_ERROR; file failures use MYYAML_STATUS_IO_ERROR.

docs.title: Handle lifetime
docs.text:
Node handles point into the owning document. A handle remains valid until the document is modified or released. Operations that grow or shrink a collection can invalidate handles to its children, so obtain a fresh handle after a mutation. myyaml_free() invalidates every handle belonging to the document.

NULL is accepted by accessors such as myyaml_node_size() and myyaml_node_type() and is reported as a null node. A NULL document handle must still not be passed to mutating functions such as myyaml_node_set_key(); those functions report MYYAML_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT.

A complete example is available in examples/apis/BasicC.c.

docs.title: Using myyaml
docs.text: This page shows the most common ways to parse, inspect, modify and emit YAML with the C++ API. The C API is covered in C API.

docs.title: Include and link
docs.text:
#include <myyaml/myyaml.hpp>

With CMake, link the Myyaml::Myyaml target:

find_package(Myyaml REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE Myyaml::Myyaml)

The C++ implementation requires C++17. The C API is a separate target, Myyaml::MyyamlC, and requires C11 or newer.

docs.title: Parse a document
docs.text:
myyaml::yaml::parse() accepts a std::string_view and returns a value. Parse errors throw myyaml::parse_error, which includes the line, column and byte offset of the failure.

#include <myyaml/myyaml.hpp>

#include <iostream>

int main()
{
    const char *text =
        "name: demo\n"
        "enabled: true\n"
        "retries: 3\n"
        "ratio: 0.75\n"
        "features: [parse, emit]\n"
        "servers:\n"
        "  - host: primary\n"
        "    port: 8080\n"
        "  - host: secondary\n"
        "    port: 8081\n";

    myyaml::yaml config = myyaml::yaml::parse(text);
    std::cout << config["name"].as_string() << '\n';
}

The parser applies the YAML 1.2 core schema to plain scalars, so true, 42, 0x2A, 3.5 and null become the corresponding boolean, integer, floating point and null values. Quoted scalars are always strings.

docs.title: Read values safely
docs.text:
Throwing accessors such as as_string() and as_integer() raise myyaml::type_error when the node has another type. Non-throwing accessors return std::optional and are convenient when the input is untrusted.

const myyaml::yaml retries = config["retries"];
if (auto value = retries.get_integer())
{
    std::cout << "retries: " << *value << '\n';
}

if (config["enabled"].get_boolean().value_or(false))
{
    std::cout << "enabled\n";
}

Use contains() or find() before indexing a mapping when the key may be missing:

if (config.contains("servers"))
{
    const myyaml::yaml &servers = config["servers"];
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < servers.size(); ++index)
    {
        std::cout << servers[index]["host"].as_string() << '\n';
    }
}

yaml::operator[](std::string_view) inserts a missing key with a null value, while yaml::at() throws myyaml::lookup_error for a missing key.

docs.title: Parse without exceptions
docs.text:
yaml::try_parse() returns a result object and never throws. This is useful in libraries that cannot use exceptions or when reporting errors to a user.

const myyaml::parse_result result = myyaml::yaml::try_parse("a: [1, 2\n");
if (result)
{
    const myyaml::yaml &document = *result.value;
    // ...
}
else
{
    std::cerr << result.error << " at line " << result.line
              << ", column " << result.column << '\n';
}

try_parse() also reports encoding errors such as invalid UTF-8 through result.error.

docs.title: Parse files and streams
docs.text:
myyaml::yaml from_file = myyaml::yaml::parse_file("config.yaml");

std::ifstream input("config.yaml");
myyaml::yaml from_stream = myyaml::yaml::parse(input);

std::FILE *file = std::fopen("config.yaml", "rb");
if (file != nullptr)
{
    myyaml::yaml from_c_stream = myyaml::yaml::parse(file);
    std::fclose(file);
}

Exceptions from I/O failures are myyaml::io_error; malformed YAML raises myyaml::parse_error. The std::istream extraction operator is also available:

std::istringstream input("name: demo\n");
myyaml::yaml document;
input >> document;

docs.title: Emit YAML
docs.text:
Every value can be serialized with dump():

const std::string text = config.dump();
std::cout << text;

myyaml::dump_options controls formatting:

myyaml::dump_options options;
options.indent = 4;              // 1..8, default 2
options.flow = false;            // true emits [a, b] / {k: v}
options.sort_keys = true;        // deterministic key order
options.explicit_start = true;   // emit "---"
options.explicit_end = true;     // emit "..."
options.trailing_newline = true; // default

std::cout << config.dump(options);

Emission can also target a stream:

config.dump(std::cout, options);
std::cout << config; // default options

The emitter quotes strings when plain scalars would change their meaning, and uses literal block scalars for multi-line text. Invalid UTF-8 is rejected with myyaml::encoding_error rather than producing a corrupt document.

docs.title: Build and modify documents
docs.text:
Start from a null value or an empty collection and build the document programmatically:

myyaml::yaml document;
document["name"] = "demo";
document["enabled"] = true;
document["ports"].push_back(8080);
document["ports"].push_back(8081);
document["limits"]["cpu"] = 2;
document["limits"]["memory"] = "4Gi";

myyaml::yaml explicit_sequence =
    myyaml::yaml::make_sequence({1, "two", false});

myyaml::yaml explicit_mapping = myyaml::yaml::make_mapping({
    {"name", "demo"},
    {"values", explicit_sequence},
});

document.erase("enabled");
document.set("updated-by", "example");

Assigning to a null node converts it to a mapping (operator[](key)) or a sequence (push_back()). Mappings preserve insertion order. Copies are deep: modifying a copy never changes the original value.

docs.title: Limits and untrusted input
docs.text:
Parser limits protect applications that process untrusted YAML:

myyaml::parse_options options;
options.max_depth = 64;                    // nesting depth
options.max_input_size = 1024 * 1024;      // 1 MiB
options.max_nodes = 100000;                // nodes including aliases
options.allow_duplicate_keys = false;      // default

myyaml::yaml document = myyaml::yaml::parse(untrusted_text, options);

Exceeding a limit raises myyaml::parse_error. See REVIEW.md for the current limitations of the parser and emitter.

docs.title: Complete example
docs.text:
examples/apis/Basic.cpp is a compilable version of the parse, read, modify and emit workflow:

cmake -S . -B build -DMYYAML_BUILD_EXAMPLES=ON
cmake --build build --target Basic
./build/examples/apis/Basic

The C equivalent is in examples/apis/BasicC.c.
